title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is a case of political deepfake impersonation, in which AI-generated video was used to put words into a real candidate's mouth. The videos were posted to a social media account by the opposing campaign, so the point of deployment was public political communication rather than any internal or commercial system. The generator applied an automatic label identifying the content as AI-made, which means the platform disclosed the synthetic origin while the false speech itself remained.

Catching this kind of use does not depend on detecting the model's output, because the label already did that. What no label can supply is consent from the person depicted or the truth of the statements attributed to her. The only checks available here are the ones the poster declined to apply and the ones the platform did not impose, such as refusing to host synthetic depictions of a named candidate.

It is not established that the videos are defamatory, that any claim will be filed, or that Van Orden intended to deceive anyone. A cease-and-desist letter is a demand, not a ruling, and the campaign's public response is a statement, not a finding.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI-generated deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden posted videos to X showing a fake version of Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip shared on Aug. 4. The videos carry an automatic label noting they were made with an AI generator called Grok Imagine.

Cooke's attorney, Ben Stafford, wrote on Sept. 30 that the content is false and aimed at harming her reputation. The letter says Van Orden could face defamation claims under state law and that Cooke's team is monitoring his accounts and weighing all legal options. Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum, and he responded with another AI video.
